rationale: Reviewed against real cross-platform CI evidence for issue #78 (PR #84, CI run https://github.com/SamuFL/RVRBoTron/actions/runs/33867625534): macOS arm64 clang, macOS Intel clang, and Windows x86_64 MSVC, both float32 and float64 presets, comparing every platform's compact tail-v2-equivalence summary of the same millisecond-scale Damping tracer (tests/test_tail_v2_equivalence_cli.py) against a macOS arm64 baseline. Every structural fact (band count, T20/T30 fit presence, withinPredictedTolerance, withinAccuracyInvariant, significantDeviation, eventualContraction.negativeTrend, dampingEnabled, gainMode, nonFiniteSampleCount, alignmentScore) reproduced with exactly zero delta on every platform and precision, same as tail_tolerances_v1.json's own findings. The float64 preset's numeric metrics also reproduced at the same tiny 1e-13-to-1e-16 scale tail_tolerances_v1.json observed, chained through the identical NumPy float64 FFT/regression/Coloration math regardless of DSP sample precision. The float32 preset told a different, genuinely new story: decayRt60Sec, decayRelativeError, eventualContractionSlopeDbPerSegment, and every Coloration metric showed materially larger cross-platform deltas (1e-7-to-1e-4 scale, not 1e-13-to-1e-16) than tail-v1's own undamped tracer ever produced under the identical code paths. This is attributed to the Damping shelf recursion itself: the boosted/attenuated spectral shape it produces makes the T20/T30 Schroeder-curve regression and the Coloration FFT summary more sensitive to the float32 DSP build's own platform-specific rounding (different compilers -- AppleClang vs. MSVC -- and SIMD codegen), not to any instability in this analyzer's own Python math (which is confirmed float64-deterministic by the float64 preset's tiny deltas, and by predictedTargetRt60Sec/predictedRangeLow/HighRt60Sec -- pure functions of resolved.json's already-double-precision coefficients -- reproducing at the same ~1e-14 scale in BOTH precision groups, unaffected by DSP sample precision at all). Each committed value below states its own observed evidence and headroom; values for the new predicted-target/range and eventual-contraction metrics were absent from tail_tolerances_v1.json entirely and are derived fresh here.

nonFiniteSampleCount.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta across macOS arm64, macOS Intel, and Windows x86_64 (CI run 33867625534) for the tracer's output.wav. A non-finite sample is a discrete numerical-hygiene failure, not a floating-point accumulation, same basis as tail_tolerances_v1.json's identical entry.

decayRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 1.82e-07 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=2000 T30 fit, CI run 33867625534) across all 9 octave bands' T20 and T30 estimates -- roughly two orders of magnitude looser than tail-v1's own float32 decayRt60Sec observation (2.66e-15), attributed to the Damping shelf recursion making the Schroeder-curve regression more sensitive to the float32 DSP build's own cross-platform rounding (see the top-level rationale), not to this analyzer's own math. Committed at 1e-4, roughly 550x that observed delta: 1e-4 seconds remains far tighter than any practically meaningful RT60 precision, while leaving headroom for configurations (steeper shelves, longer renders) this tiny tracer does not exercise.

predictedTargetRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.01e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=125, CI run 33867625534). A pure function of resolved.json's already-double-precision shelf coefficients (cos/sin/log10 chained in Python float64), independent of DSP sample precision -- confirmed by the float64 preset observing the identical ~1e-14 scale. Committed at 1e-9, matching tail_tolerances_v1.json's own decayRt60Sec headroom philosophy for cross-platform libm variance.

predictedRangeLowRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.02e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=63, CI run 33867625534); see predictedTargetRt60Sec, the per-Channel minimum of the same computation.

predictedRangeHighRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.82e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=125, CI run 33867625534); see predictedTargetRt60Sec, the per-Channel maximum of the same computation.

decayRelativeError.rationale: Observed max delta 1.41e-07 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534): a ratio of two decayRt60Sec-scale quantities (measured vs. requested), so the same evidence and headroom basis as decayRt60Sec above.

eventualContractionSlopeDbPerSegment.rationale: Observed max delta 2.79e-07 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534): a linear-regression slope over per-segment log-energy, chaining the same float32-DSP-sensitive Schroeder/regression machinery as decayRt60Sec. Committed at 1e-4, the same headroom philosophy.

alignmentScore.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta on all three platforms, confirming the design expectation -- Alignment is a discrete Jaccard overlap of active-frame sets, not a floating-point accumulation, same basis as tail_tolerances_v1.json's identical entry.

colorationPeakToPeakDb.rationale: Observed max delta 7.61e-05 dB (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534) -- materially larger than tail_tolerances_v1.json's own float32 colorationPeakToPeakDb observation (exactly 0), attributed to the Damping shelf reshaping the spectrum in a way that is more sensitive to the float32 DSP build's own cross-platform rounding (see the top-level rationale), the same underlying cause as decayRt60Sec's own new headroom. Committed at 1e-3 dB, roughly 13x that observed delta and far below any audible significance.

colorationRmsDb.rationale: Observed max delta 1.10e-09 dB (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534). Committed at 1e-6, roughly 900x that observed delta; same underlying cause as colorationPeakToPeakDb but a materially smaller effect on this smoother, more-averaged metric.

colorationSpectralFlatness.rationale: Observed max delta 1.11e-09 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534). Committed at 1e-6, roughly 900x that observed delta; see colorationRmsDb.

nonFiniteSampleCount.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta between macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64 (macOS Intel does not build the double preset, CI run 33867625534); same basis as the float32 entry.

decayRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 3.77e-15 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=250 T20 fit, CI run 33867625534) -- the same tiny scale tail_tolerances_v1.json's own float64 decayRt60Sec entry observed (1.11e-15), confirming the float32 preset's much larger delta is specifically a float32-DSP-build effect, not a defect in the T20/T30 fit itself. Committed at 1e-9, matching tail_tolerances_v1.json's own value.

predictedTargetRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.01e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=125, CI run 33867625534) -- identical to the float32 preset's own observation, confirming this metric is independent of DSP sample precision (see the float32 entry).

predictedRangeLowRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.02e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=63, CI run 33867625534); see the float32 entry.

predictedRangeHighRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.82e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, band=125, CI run 33867625534); see the float32 entry.

decayRelativeError.rationale: Observed max delta 2.96e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534); see the float32 entry and decayRt60Sec above.

eventualContractionSlopeDbPerSegment.rationale: Observed max delta 1.05e-13 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534) -- the same tiny scale as decayRt60Sec's float64 entry, confirming the float32 preset's much larger delta is a float32-DSP-build effect.

alignmentScore.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta between macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64, confirming the design expectation; same basis as the float32 entry.

colorationPeakToPeakDb.rationale: Observed max delta 1.07e-13 dB (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534) -- close to tail_tolerances_v1.json's own float64 colorationPeakToPeakDb tolerance (1e-12), confirming the float32 preset's much larger delta is specifically a float32-DSP-build effect. Committed at 1e-9 for consistency with this file's other float64 entries.

colorationRmsDb.rationale: Observed max delta 3.55e-15 dB (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534). Committed at 1e-9 for consistency with this file's other float64 entries.

colorationSpectralFlatness.rationale: Observed max delta 4.79e-16 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64 baseline, CI run 33867625534). Committed at 1e-9 for consistency with this file's other float64 entries.
